slo_title: Explain swapping, demand paging, and copy-on-write mechanisms

mcq.q: In demand paging, the page replacement algorithm is triggered by:

options.B: Only one process runs at a time
options.C: There is memory contention and multiprogramming

mcq.answer_text: There is memory contention and multiprogramming

mcq.q: Which of the following statements about virtual memory is TRUE?

options.A: It reduces the need for page replacement
options.B: It allows each process to have its own address space
options.D: It cannot be used with paging

mcq.answer_text: It allows each process to have its own address space

sq.q: What is demand paging? How is it different from regular paging?
answer: Demand paging loads a page into memory only when it is needed (i.e., on a page fault). In regular paging, all required pages may be loaded in advance. Mark Allocation:
Demand paging loads a page into memory only when it is needed (i.e., on a page fault). In regular paging, all required pages may be loaded in advance.

sq.q: Define virtual memory. How does it work with paging?
answer: Virtual memory is a technique that allows execution of processes that may not be fully loaded into physical memory . It uses paging to map virtual addresses to physical frames, with the help of page tables and secondary storage for pages not currently in RAM. Mark Allocation:
